column15: Verified via Shin Group (the brand's global distributor/importer, fetched directly): Shinobu Distillery of Niigata Beer Co, Japan; blended whisky (50% malt/50% grain), matured/finished in Japan incl. Mizunara oak. Shin Group's own catalogue lists Shinobu and Shin but not Fujimi or Reki (also in this batch), so the seed's hypothesis tying Fujimi to this cluster is not confirmed (see fujimi row). No peat information found; left unknown.

Kind/country/region/owner/type verified via Wikipedia. Peat corrected from the seed's light to unknown: this round's rule requires a producer-domain page (or Islay) for any positive level, and Springbank is Campbeltown, not Islay; springbank.scot returned 403 this session. withheld peat proposal: medium (scotchwhisky.com Whiskypedia describes it as medium-peated at 8-10ppm) vs light (several retailers describe ~12-15ppm as lightly peated) -- sources disagree on the light/medium boundary; a human with access to the distillery's own site should resolve it. Distinct from sibling Longrow (heavy) and Hazelburn (unpeated, not in this batch).

Milestone Beverages' 'molecular whiskey' brand: a Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey core plus lab-finished flavored variants (Apple, Peach, Banana) marketed as flavored whiskey -- one retailer labels the banana variant a 'Whisky Spirit Drink' (an EU category for flavored spirits, not whisky proper). Catalogue samples are mostly the flavored line. Kept rather than rejected since a genuine bourbon anchors the range, per the brief's own when-in-doubt guidance. Kind corrected blend->brand (an engineered multi-expression brand, not a blended-whisky identity). countryCode left empty: Milestone is Hong Kong-based (the marketing company, not a whisky-producing country) and the catalogued flavored SKUs don't state a base-spirit origin. peat=none per ordinary-bourbon default; confidence stays low given the unusual production method and the flavored-vs-whisky ambiguity.

Re-confirmed this session: a 5/12-year blended Scotch bottled as 'BG&B Red Stripe' by Block, Grey & Block Ltd (Mayfair, London), 43% vol, 1970s-era lineage. Both whiskybase.com and whiskyauctioneer.com returned 403/406 to direct fetch this session; the facts above come from search-result synthesis of those exact pages rather than a page rendered myself, so confidence stays low despite the citations, matching the seed's own reasoning. No peat/smoke mentioned; peat=none per ordinary-blended-Scotch convention.

Verified via Matsui Shuzo's own site (fetched directly): The Tottori is a blended (malt+grain) Japanese whisky, sourced/aged/proofed at Matsui Shuzo, Tottori Prefecture, with Mt. Daisen spring water. No peat/smoke mentioned on the producer's own pages; one third-party review mentions 'soft smoke' in tasting notes only, too weak and non-producer to act on -- left unknown.

Private-label single malt range (Speyside and Highland bottlings, plus a Peated SKU) bottled by First Blending Co. Owner triangulated: both retailer pages list First Blending Co alongside Label 5 and Glen Turner, and La Martiniquaise's own Wikipedia page confirms Label 5 and Glen Turner are its brands, so First Blending Co is a La Martiniquaise bottling arm. Corrected kind blend->brand (a multi-expression single malt range, not one blend) and defaultTypeName empty->single malt (every known bottling is a single malt). Base peat left unknown; the Wilton House Peated SKU's specific level could not be confirmed from a producer-domain source this session (only retailer copy), so no rule.tsv exception was written -- a human should chase First Blending Co / La Martiniquaise directly for it.

Kind/country/owner/type confirmed via Wikipedia: Nikka's original 1934 Hokkaido single malt distillery, coal-fired direct-flame stills. Peat corrected from the seed's medium to unknown per this round's strict rule (positive claim needs producer-domain evidence or Islay); Yoichi is neither, and nikka.com returned 403 this session on both the distillery page and site root. withheld peat proposal: medium-to-heavy -- Yoichi is traditionally described as Nikka's peatier/smokier malt versus Miyagikyo; the only reachable corroboration is a Nonjatta blog post title referencing Yoichi 12 alongside both fruit and peat notes (real but weak, third-party). One of this batch's highest-value rows per the brief -- a human reviewer with access to Nikka's official site or a strong retailer (distiller.com, dekanta.com, whisky.com, masterofmalt.com all blocked this session too) should set the level.

Unresolved, matching the seed. Catalogue itself is inconsistent (DE/blend, US/rye, US/blend across three listings of the same name); countryCode=US kept only as the seed's own majority-vote guess, not a confirmed fact. This session's shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before this row could be searched (only a dead-end Wikipedia title guess was possible, 404); flagged as this batch's weakest row for a human to search properly with a fresh budget.

Confirmed: Bradan Orach is Speyburn's NAS entry-level single malt (named in its Wikipedia awards section), Speyburn is Inver House Distillers' Rothes, Moray (Speyside) distillery. Speyburn's own site (fetched) markets it as 'smooth' with no peat mentioned; peat=none per the verified regional convention that Speyside distilleries are typically unpeated. Confidence raised to high (was low in the seed) now that the parent distillery's own site has been checked.

Iowa craft distillery (Swisher); range spans bourbon and wheat whiskey per samples, so defaultTypeName stays empty. Could not reach a distillery-specific source this session: cedarridgewinery.com now redirects to a domain-for-sale parking page (the business may have rebranded, or the old domain simply lapsed -- worth a human checking current status), cedarridgedistillery.com returned 403, and no Wikipedia article exists under that or nearby titles. peat=none kept per the general non-Scotch convention, now backed by a page actually opened this session (the Irish whiskey Wikipedia article notes peat is seldom used in malting outside Scotland) rather than the seed's oddly-placed citation of the same page.

Mass-market blended Scotch; ownership still not verified this session. Chivas Brothers' own Wikipedia page lists its blended-Scotch portfolio (100 Pipers, Ballantine's, Chivas Regal, Long John, Passport, Royal Salute, Something Special) and Clan Campbell is not on it, ruling out that specific hypothesis; owner left empty rather than guessed, as in the seed. peat=none per the verified regional convention (Islay=heavy peat, Speyside/Lowland=typically unpeated; the Scotch whisky Wikipedia article notes blended Scotch aims for a consistent house style across its constituent whiskies rather than a dominant peat character).

Verified via the distillery's own site (clonakiltydistillery.ie, not reached by the seed round): County Cork craft distillery, B Corp certified, range spans Single Pot Still, Double Oak, Galley Head Single Malt and Port Cask -- confirms defaultTypeName correctly stays empty (multi-type range), matching the seed. No peat mentioned on their own site; peat=none per the verified Irish-whiskey convention (peat is seldom used in malting outside Scotland). Confidence raised to high (was low in the seed).

John Crabbie & Co blended Scotch. Crabbie's own Wikipedia page confirms a historical 'Crabbie's whisky business' alongside its better-known ginger wine/ginger beer, and Halewood International's page confirms Halewood bought the Crabbie's ginger-wine brand from Glenmorangie in 2002 -- but neither page confirms who currently holds the WHISKY line specifically, so owner is left empty rather than guessed, matching the seed. 'Crabbie and Cree'/'Crabbie&Cree' sample remains unresolved (possibly a gift-set SKU name). peat=none per ordinary-blend convention.

Confirmed via Wikipedia: blended Canadian whisky (rye/maize/barley), created by Seagram, owned by Diageo since 2000; distilled Gimli Manitoba, blended/bottled Amherstburg Ontario and Valleyfield Quebec. No peat/smoke mentioned; peat=none, standard for Canadian whisky. Confidence raised to high (was low in the seed, whose second citation -- the Irish whiskey page -- was an unrelated copy/paste, no longer needed now that the Crown Royal article itself was opened directly).

No producer-specific source found this session either -- an own-label blend named for a place near Edinburgh, presumably a supermarket/private-label range given the three cask-finish samples (Bourbon/Rum/Sherry Cask). peat=none per the verified ordinary-blended-Scotch convention only; identity/ownership remain unconfirmed, so confidence stays low as in the seed.

Confirmed via Lux Row Distillers' own site: Daviess County bourbon, variants Kentucky Straight (core), Cabernet Sauvignon Finish, French Oak Barrel Finished, Medium Toasted Barrel Finished -- all bourbon, so defaultTypeName=bourbon. No peat mentioned; peat=none, standard bourbon convention. Added a new lux-row-distillers row (see below) since it was not in live-slugs.txt or any input row and this row's bottlerSlug needs it. Confidence raised to high (was low in the seed).

No web presence found this session either, matching the seed exactly. Single sample name, no further detail available. peat=none kept only as the verified ordinary-blended-Scotch category default; identity remains unconfirmed.

Confirmed via English and French Wikipedia: Le Lay family's Distillerie des Menhirs, Plomelin, Brittany, France -- makers of what they describe as the first pure buckwheat whisky (1998), double-distilled in a direct-flame pot still, aged in French oak; range includes Diamant/Gold/Silver/Broceliande (pure buckwheat), Grey Rock (blended), Ed Gwenn (single grain). Buckwheat whisky is outside the closed defaultTypeName list so left empty, as in the seed. For a human reviewer: the French Wikipedia article also mentions limited-edition 'peated versions' exist in the wider range, but gives no level, and the official site (distillerie-des-menhirs.com, with and without www) fails DNS resolution -- none of this batch's Eddu samples are named Peated, so peatProfile=none is kept here and no rule.tsv exception was written for the unconfirmed peated editions.

Could not reach a producer-specific source this session: eganswhiskey.com (403), eganswhiskey.ie and egans-irish-whiskey.com (DNS failures), masterofmalt.com/whiskies/egans/ (403 on retry). General knowledge points to P.&H. Egan Ltd (Tullamore) as the historic family name, but this remains unconfirmed by any page opened this session, so owner stays empty and kind stays blend, matching the seed. Range (Vintage Grain, Fortitude, Legacy Reserve Series III) suggests a multi-style range; defaultTypeName left empty. peat=none per the verified Irish-whiskey convention only.

Confirmed via both sources (fetched directly): blended Irish whiskey, 80% bourbon-cask single grain / 20% single malt, triple distilled, Co. Cork, minimum 4 years, 40% ABV; producer named as Hyde Distillery (matches the seed's fuller 'Hyde Irish Whiskey / Hibernia Distillers'). No peat/smoke mentioned (vanilla/honey/toasted-oak tasting notes); peat=none. Confidence raised to high (was low in the seed).

Confirmed via the brand's own site: French single malt (launched 2019), exclusively French raw materials, non-chill-filtered, distilled at Distillerie Hepp (Alsace) -- so kind corrected distillery->brand (Whiskies Du Monde is the brand; Hepp is the physical distillery). The base Evade/Evade Single Malt range is unpeated; a separate Evade Single Malt Peated (43%) exists but the page gives no specific level (no ppm, no light/medium/heavy wording), so no rule.tsv exception was written for it -- flagged for a human to chase directly with Whiskies Du Monde. Accented spelling is Evade with an acute accent; catalogue spells it unaccented, matching the seed's note.

Confirmed via the distillery's own site: family-owned 'warm distillery' since 1880, Deinze, Belgium (primarily jenever/gin, also bottles whisky). Corrected defaultTypeName single malt->empty: the same site also lists a Single Rye Whisky (100% rye) alongside the Single Malt (100% sherry-cask-aged), so the range is not uniformly one type -- see flavor.tsv for the sherry house style on the single malt line. No peat mentioned. Confidence raised to high (matches the seed's own citation, now independently reopened).

Neither of this batch's two hypotheses for Fujimi panned out this session: Shin Group's own catalogue (which does list its Shinobu sibling) has no Fujimi product, and Matsui Shuzo's own site has no Fujimi product either (checked its Tottori category page and a direct /fujimi/ guess, both without it, and a platinaliquor.com guess 403'd). Sample 'Fujimi Matsui Distillery' remains unexplained -- possibly a mislabeled/parsed name, or a genuinely obscure brand this session's tools (WebSearch budget exhausted) could not reach. Left unresolved, matching the seed.

New row for daviess-county (its bottlerSlug reference; lux-row-distillers was not in live-slugs.txt or any input row). Confirmed via the distillery's own site: Luxco-owned bourbon distillery, Bardstown, Kentucky, opened 2018; also produces Rebel Bourbon, Ezra Brooks, David Nicholson and Blood Oath. No peat mentioned; peat=none per the bourbon-category convention (matches every other US bourbon row in this batch).
